subject.title: fix(sqlite): repair canonical indexes before database use

question: Should OpenClaw adopt schema-derived repair of every canonical named SQLite index at database-open time, including the specified fail-closed handling for unexpected unique constraints?
rationale: This changes upgrade-sensitive persistent-state recovery semantics across both global and per-agent databases; the intended repair and quarantine boundary is a maintainer-owned product and data-safety decision.

options.title: Approve the schema-derived repair boundary
options.body: Accept canonical schema SQL as the sole named-index registry after confirming the migration deferral and corruption quarantine behavior are intentional.

options.title: Narrow repair to known recoverable cases
options.body: Retain the prior narrower behavior if maintainers prefer explicit allowlists over repairing all schema-derived named indexes during open.

recommendation.title: Approve the schema-derived repair boundary
recommendation.body: Accept canonical schema SQL as the sole named-index registry after confirming the migration deferral and corruption quarantine behavior are intentional.

likelyOwner.reason: The current member-authored patch and supplied evidence place this contributor closest to the implementation and intended SQLite recovery semantics.
